result:
Nothing is built yet, so this goes through New-Project Entry. There's no spec: `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` is a research brief, and the three research files are background. So every outcome below is a **candidate** taken from those files, for you to confirm. No file in `specs/` carries a roadmap header, and `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md` doesn't exist.

I read only the opening ~3,000 characters of each research file. The cost notes rest on those excerpts and on public facts, and are marked where only a real run can tell.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | History of revision size (mean absolute revision and tails) for total nonfarm, at each revision step and by era: 1st→2nd print, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, post-benchmark | prompt Part A; chatgpt §1.2 | Small. BLS publishes 1st/2nd/3rd-print revision tables back to 1979, and benchmark articles are annual. Hours of your time, megabytes of data. |
| O2 | Whether the collection interval (days from the 12th to first closing) and the first-closing rate predict the size of the one-month revision | prompt driver 2; chatgpt §2.2, §3.2 | Collection days come from the calendar and release dates, so they are cheap. Closing rates come from BLS tables, and how far back they go is unknown. Fit cost is measured by running it. |
| O3 | Split of the 1st→2nd and 2nd→3rd SA revisions into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part, from SA and NSA vintages together | prompt driver 1, Part C; chatgpt §4.5 | Depends on NSA vintage coverage in ALFRED or archived releases, which I haven't verified. A one-series probe would firm this up. |
| O4 | Size of the benchmark revision and the wedge-back pattern, with birth–death error, by supersector | prompt Part A stages 3–4; chatgpt §2.6, §4.6 | About 40 annual benchmark articles, partly hand-extracted. Supersector vintage depth is unknown. |
| O5 | What funding, staffing and sample size can and cannot say about revision size, with shrinkage priors (party control shown only as a descriptive grouping) | prompt drivers 3–5; claude §4.7 | Mostly your time. Appropriations and FTE counts are hand-built from about 40 years of budget justifications and FedScope: days, not hours. |
| O6 | The full multi-vintage state-space model: latent employment path, news and noise across all four revision steps, stochastic volatility with covariates in the log-scale, Student-t errors, supersector hierarchy, structural change | prompt Part C; all three designs | NUTS compute is unknown until a fit is timed. It is probably the dominant compute cost by far. |
| O7 | Evidence that the covariate-scale model beats a constant-variance baseline: LOO/PSIS and pseudo-real-time checks | prompt Part C, Validation | Multiplies O6's fit cost by the number of pseudo-real-time refits, which only a run can measure. |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: manifests, traceability, point-in-time awareness, full validation suites, scheduling.

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Revision-size history** (O1), known progression. It is descriptive and needs no model.
- **B: Collection interval** (O2), research. Split from C because the collection-interval answer stands without the seasonal decomposition, and it has the sharpest variation within a year.
- **C: Seasonal vs. sample** (O3), research. Split from B for the same reason. It also depends on NSA vintage availability, which B doesn't need.
- **D: Benchmark and wedge-back** (O4), research. A different revision step, data source (QCEW) and timing from B and C.
- **E: Operational capacity** (O5), research. Split off so that hand-building budget data doesn't hold up B to D. Its answer stands alone, and it may come back as "not identified".
- **F: Joint model** (O6, O7), research. This is the integrating design rather than an unrelated question. I'm proposing it as its own track so it can draw on what B to E learn. Tell me if you'd rather fold it in elsewhere.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, managed with uv (`.python-version`, `uv.lock`).
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax only where a custom kernel is warranted, ArviZ, and Polars (prompt, Part C implementation notes).
- National CES all-employees, with supersector detail where it identifies mechanisms (chatgpt scope line).

Proposed roadmap name: `ces-revisions`, which gives `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`.

## One request

Please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves. Then confirm or change the tracks, their kinds, and the name.

If you'd like, in the same reply say yes to one small probe: listing ALFRED vintages for total nonfarm SA and NSA (`PAYEMS` / `PAYNSA`) to firm up the O1 and O3 cost notes.
